source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הָרְבִיעִ֔ת לִיהוֹיָקִ֥ים בֶּן־יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה הָיָ֞ה הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in the year the fourth of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, came the word this to Jeremiah from with Yahweh, saying:

en.L: And it was in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, [that] this word came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying:
en.B: This message came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the fourth year of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
en.R: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah this message:

decisions.choice: the fourth year of Jehoiakim: 605 BC, the year of 25:1
decisions.reason: Jehoiakim became king in 609 BC, so his fourth year was 605 BC, the year Nebuchadrezzar defeated Egypt at Carchemish and became king of Babylon (25:1; 46:2). The short word to Baruch in 45:1 is dated to this same year, "when he wrote these words in a scroll at Jeremiah's dictation".

decisions.choice: chapter 36 of the Hebrew is chapter 43 of the Greek translation
decisions.reason: Because the Greek translation (the Septuagint) places the oracles against the nations after 25:13, this chapter stands later there (see 1:1). The Greek of this chapter is also somewhat shorter. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: the word came ... saying: the heading of a new account, told about Jeremiah rather than by him
decisions.reason: The chapter is a narrative in the third person, like chapters 26 and 28. "Saying" introduces the LORD's command in verses 2-3.

decisions.choice: this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying: (L); This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD (B); the LORD gave Jeremiah this message (R)
decisions.reason: The heading is worded as the book's settled formula for "the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD", with "this" kept from the Hebrew.

source.text: קַח־לְךָ֮ מְגִלַּת־סֵפֶר֒ וְכָתַבְתָּ֣ אֵלֶ֗יהָ אֵ֣ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֞ים אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֧רְתִּי אֵלֶ֛יךָ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל וְעַל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וְעַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם מִיּ֞וֹם דִּבַּ֤רְתִּי אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ מִימֵ֣י יֹאשִׁיָּ֔הוּ וְעַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Take for yourself [a] scroll of [a] book and write on it all the words that I have spoken to you concerning Israel and concerning Judah and concerning all the nations, from [the] day I spoke to you, from [the] days of Josiah, and until the day this.

en.L: "Take for yourself a scroll of a book and write on it all the words that I have spoken to you concerning Israel and concerning Judah and concerning all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah, until this day.
en.B: "Take a scroll and write on it every word that I have spoken to you about Israel, about Judah and about all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you in the days of Josiah until today.
en.R: "Get a scroll and write on it everything I have told you about Israel, about Judah and about all the other nations. Write down all I have said from the time I first spoke to you, when Josiah was king, until now.

decisions.choice: a scroll of a book: a scroll made for writing a document
decisions.reason: A scroll was a long strip of leather or papyrus sheets joined together and rolled up. The second word means a written document; joined to "scroll" it says what the roll is for. The same two words return in verse 4, and later verses say simply "the scroll".

decisions.choice: from the days of Josiah: from Jeremiah's call in Josiah's thirteenth year, 627 BC
decisions.reason: Jeremiah began to prophesy in the thirteenth year of Josiah (1:2), some twenty-three years before this command (25:3). The scroll is to hold the whole of his message up to now.

decisions.choice: concerning: about, and in most of the words against, Israel, Judah and the nations
decisions.reason: The small word can mean "about" or "against". Most of what Jeremiah had spoken was warning of judgment, but the scroll also held his calls to turn back (verse 3).

decisions.choice: Israel: the Greek translation reads "Jerusalem"
decisions.reason: The Septuagint has "concerning Jerusalem and concerning Judah". The Hebrew "Israel" fits Jeremiah's early words to the northern tribes (3:6-13) and to the whole people. The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: first (Balanced, Readable); other nations (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "first" to make clear that the day meant is the day of Jeremiah's call. Readable adds "other" because Israel and Judah are nations too.

source.text: אוּלַ֤י יִשְׁמְעוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה אֵ֚ת כָּל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י חֹשֵׁ֖ב לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָהֶ֑ם לְמַ֣עַן יָשׁ֗וּבוּ אִ֚ישׁ מִדַּרְכּ֣וֹ הָרָעָ֔ה וְסָלַחְתִּ֥י לַעֲוֺנָ֖ם וּלְחַטָּאתָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Perhaps will hear [the] house of Judah all the evil that I [am] planning to do to them, so that they may turn, each from his way the evil, and I will forgive their iniquity and their sin.

en.L: Perhaps the house of Judah will hear all the evil that I am planning to do to them, so that they turn back, each [one] from {{gender:their|his}} evil way, and I will forgive their iniquity and their sin."
en.B: It may be that when the house of Judah hears about all the disaster I intend to bring on them, every one of them will turn back from their evil way, and I will forgive their guilt and their sin."
en.R: Maybe when the people of Judah hear about all the terrible things I plan to do to them, each of them will turn away from their evil way of life. Then I will forgive their sin and all the wrong they have done."

decisions.choice: the evil I am planning: disaster, set against the people's evil way
decisions.reason: The same word names the harm the LORD plans and the wrong the people do. The disaster answers their evil; if they turn from their evil, the disaster can be turned aside (18:8; 26:3).

decisions.choice: perhaps ... so that they turn ... and I will forgive: the writing is a last call to repent
decisions.reason: The LORD does not say they will listen, but he leaves room for it. The scroll is meant to bring the people back and so to bring forgiveness, not only to record a sentence. Verse 31 says they did not listen.

decisions.choice: iniquity and sin: two words for wrongdoing, together meaning all their guilt
decisions.reason: The first word names wrongdoing with the guilt it brings, the second a failing or offense. Paired, they cover the whole of what needs forgiving.

decisions.choice: the evil (L); disaster, terrible things (B, R); iniquity (L), guilt (B), sin (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "evil" twice to show the play on words (m1); Balanced and Readable say "disaster" for the harm the LORD plans. The word for iniquity follows the wording used for Isaiah. Readable says "the people of Judah" for "the house of Judah". Literal uses a gender setting because the whole people, women and men, is meant.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֣א יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ אֶת־בָּר֖וּךְ בֶּן־נֵֽרִיָּ֑ה וַיִּכְתֹּ֨ב בָּר֜וּךְ מִפִּ֣י יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ אֵ֣ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֧י יְהוָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלָ֖יו עַל־מְגִלַּת־סֵֽפֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And called Jeremiah Baruch son of Neriah, and wrote Baruch from [the] mouth of Jeremiah all [the] words of Yahweh that he had spoken to him on [a] scroll of [a] book.

en.L: And Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken to him, on a scroll of a book.
en.B: So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and as Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote down on a scroll everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to him.
en.R: So Jeremiah sent for Baruch son of Neriah. Jeremiah spoke all the words {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given him, and Baruch wrote them down on a scroll.

decisions.choice: from the mouth of Jeremiah: at Jeremiah's dictation
decisions.reason: To write "from the mouth of" someone is to write down what he says aloud (verses 6, 17-18, 27, 32). The words are the LORD's, spoken to Jeremiah; Jeremiah speaks them, and Baruch writes.

decisions.choice: Baruch son of Neriah: Jeremiah's scribe and companion
decisions.reason: Baruch had signed and kept the deed of Jeremiah's field (32:12-16), went with him to Egypt (43:3-6), and received a word of his own from the LORD (45:1-5). His brother Seraiah served King Zedekiah (51:59).

decisions.choice: as Jeremiah dictated (Balanced); Jeremiah spoke ... and Baruch wrote them down (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m1); Literal keeps "from the mouth of".

source.text: וַיְצַוֶּ֣ה יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ אֶת־בָּר֖וּךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר אֲנִ֣י עָצ֔וּר לֹ֣א אוּכַ֔ל לָב֖וֹא בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded Jeremiah Baruch, saying, I [am] restrained; not I am able to go [into the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, "I [am] restrained; I am not able to go into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then Jeremiah gave Baruch these instructions: "I am barred; I cannot go into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then Jeremiah told Baruch, "I have been kept away. I am not allowed to go into {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple.

decisions.choice: restrained: kept from going, not shut up in prison
decisions.reason: The word means held back or shut in. Elsewhere it is used of Jeremiah confined in the court of the guard (33:1; 39:15), but here he is free to go into hiding (verses 19, 26). The reason he was barred from the temple is not given; it may have been a ban after his temple sermon (26:7-11) or after Pashhur had him beaten and put in the stocks (20:1-3), or some passing hindrance.

decisions.choice: I am restrained; I cannot go: the reason Baruch must go in his place
decisions.reason: The two clauses explain the command of verse 6, where the "you" is stressed: you go, since I cannot.

decisions.choice: barred (Balanced); kept away (Readable)
decisions.reason: These words say that Jeremiah was prevented from going without suggesting he was in prison (m1). Readable says "temple" for the house of the LORD, as it does throughout.

source.text: וּבָאתָ֣ אַתָּ֡ה וְקָרָ֣אתָ בַמְּגִלָּ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־כָּתַֽבְתָּ־מִפִּי֩ אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה בְּאָזְנֵ֥י הָעָ֛ם בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה בְּי֣וֹם צ֑וֹם וְגַ֨ם בְּאָזְנֵ֧י כָל־יְהוּדָ֛ה הַבָּאִ֥ים מֵעָרֵיהֶ֖ם תִּקְרָאֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And go you and read in the scroll which you have written from my mouth the words of Yahweh in [the] ears of the people [in the] house of Yahweh on [a] day of fasting; and also in [the] ears of all Judah the coming from their cities you shall read them.

en.L: So you go, and read from the scroll that you have written from my mouth the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the ears of the people in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on a day of fasting; and also in the ears of all Judah who come from their cities you shall read them.
en.B: So you must go, and on a fast day read the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the scroll you wrote at my dictation, in the hearing of the people in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Read them also in the hearing of all the people of Judah who come in from their towns.
en.R: So you go to the temple on a day when the people are fasting. Read the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the scroll that you wrote as I spoke. Read them to the people there, and to all the people of Judah who come in from their towns.

decisions.choice: you: stressed, you in my place
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out, which in Hebrew gives it weight. Because Jeremiah cannot go (verse 5), Baruch must go for him.

decisions.choice: in the ears of: aloud, so that they hear
decisions.reason: To read "in the ears of" people is to read to them aloud. The phrase returns through the chapter (verses 10, 13-15, 20-21).

decisions.choice: a day of fasting: a day called for prayer in time of danger, when crowds came to the temple
decisions.reason: A public fast was proclaimed when the people faced disaster, and people came in from the towns to pray (verse 9; 14:12; Joel 1:14). On such a day the largest crowd would hear the words.

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: The word for "cities" covers walled places of every size. Balanced and Readable say "towns" for the places of Judah outside Jerusalem. Readable puts the reading in the temple first and says "as I spoke" for "from my mouth".

source.text: אוּלַ֞י תִּפֹּ֤ל תְּחִנָּתָם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְיָשֻׁ֕בוּ אִ֖ישׁ מִדַּרְכּ֣וֹ הָרָעָ֑ה כִּֽי־גָד֤וֹל הָאַף֙ וְהַ֣חֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Perhaps will fall their supplication before Yahweh and they will turn, each from his way the evil, for great [is] the anger and the wrath that has spoken Yahweh against the people this.

en.L: Perhaps their supplication will fall before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they will turn back, each [one] from {{gender:their|his}} evil way, for great [is] the anger and the wrath that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken against this people."
en.B: It may be that their plea for mercy will come before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and every one of them will turn back from their evil way. For the anger and fury that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has declared against this people are great."
en.R: Maybe they will humbly ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for mercy, and each of them will turn away from their evil way of life. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is very angry with these people, and that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fury is great."

decisions.choice: their supplication will fall before the LORD: their humble plea will come before him and be heard
decisions.reason: A plea that "falls before" someone is laid down before him humbly, as a person falls down before a king, in hope that it will be accepted. The same phrase returns in 37:20 and 42:2, 9.

decisions.choice: the anger and the wrath: two words together for burning fury
decisions.reason: The first word is anger, pictured as a flaring nose; the second is heat, rage. Together they stress how great the danger is, which is why the people must plead.

decisions.choice: perhaps: the plea and the turning go together
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, the hope is that the people will both pray and change their ways. Jeremiah repeats the LORD's "perhaps" in his own words.

decisions.choice: the LORD has said that he is very angry ... and that his fury is great
decisions.reason: Readable puts "the anger ... that the LORD has spoken" as a plain statement of what the LORD has said.

source.text: וַיַּ֗עַשׂ בָּרוּךְ֙ בֶּן־נֵ֣רִיָּ֔ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֖הוּ יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא לִקְרֹ֥א בַסֵּ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בֵּ֥ית יְהֹוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And did Baruch son of Neriah according to all that commanded him Jeremiah the prophet, to read in the book [the] words of Yahweh [in the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And Baruch son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading from the scroll the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Baruch son of Neriah did everything the prophet Jeremiah had commanded him: he read the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the scroll in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Baruch son of Neriah did everything the prophet Jeremiah told him to do. He read the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the scroll in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple.

decisions.choice: a summary: verses 9-10 tell in full what this verse tells in brief
decisions.reason: The verse sums up Baruch's obedience; the next verses give the date and the place of the reading, about a year after the writing (verses 1, 9).

decisions.choice: the book: the scroll Baruch had written
decisions.reason: The word for "book" means any written document; here and in verses 10-11 it is the scroll of verse 2.

decisions.choice: scroll
decisions.reason: "Book" would make a modern reader think of bound pages. Every level says "scroll" for this word wherever it means the roll Baruch wrote.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַ֠חֲמִשִׁית לִיהוֹיָקִ֨ים בֶּן־יֹאשִׁיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַתְּשִׁעִ֔י קָרְא֨וּ צ֜וֹם לִפְנֵ֧י יְהוָ֛ה כָּל־הָעָ֖ם בִּירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְכָל־הָעָ֗ם הַבָּאִ֛ים מֵעָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in the year the fifth of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the month the ninth, they proclaimed [a] fast before Yahweh, all the people in Jerusalem and all the people the coming from [the] cities of Judah into Jerusalem.

en.L: And it was in the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, [that] they proclaimed a fast before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all the people in Jerusalem and all the people who came from the cities of Judah into Jerusalem.
en.B: In the ninth month of the fifth year of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, a fast was proclaimed before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for all the people in Jerusalem and for all the people who came into Jerusalem from the towns of Judah.
en.R: In the ninth month of the fifth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, a fast to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was announced. It was for all the people in Jerusalem, and for all who came into Jerusalem from the towns of Judah.

decisions.choice: the ninth month of the fifth year: about December 604 BC
decisions.reason: The ninth month (Kislev) falls in November and December, in the cold rainy season (verse 22). The reading took place more than a year after the LORD's command to write (verse 1).

decisions.choice: a fast proclaimed: a day of prayer called in a time of danger
decisions.reason: The text does not say why the fast was called. In that same month Nebuchadrezzar's army captured Ashkelon on the coast of Philistia, as a Babylonian record of his reign tells, and Judah may have feared it was next. Drought is another possible reason (14:1, 12).

decisions.choice: all the people: those for whom the fast was proclaimed
alternatives: all the people proclaimed a fast
decisions.reason: The verb "they proclaimed" has no named subject; the leaders called the fast. "All the people" are most likely the ones it was called for, though the words can also be read as the people themselves proclaiming it. Either way the whole city and its visitors were there.

decisions.choice: a fast ... was proclaimed for all the people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a passive verb, since no subject is named, and say who the fast was for (m3). Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א בָר֥וּךְ בַּסֵּ֛פֶר אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה בְּלִשְׁכַּ֡ת גְּמַרְיָהוּ֩ בֶן־שָׁפָ֨ן הַסֹּפֵ֜ר בֶּחָצֵ֣ר הָעֶלְי֗וֹן פֶּ֣תַח שַׁ֤עַר בֵּית־יְהוָה֙ הֶֽחָדָ֔שׁ בְּאָזְנֵ֖י כָּל־הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And read Baruch in the book the words of Jeremiah [in the] house of Yahweh in [the] chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe in the court the upper, [at the] entrance of [the] gate of [the] house of Yahweh the new, in [the] ears of all the people.

en.L: And Baruch read from the scroll the words of Jeremiah in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court, at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in the ears of all the people.
en.B: Then Baruch read the words of Jeremiah from the scroll in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in the hearing of all the people. He read from the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the secretary, in the upper courtyard, at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Baruch read Jeremiah's words from the scroll in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, so that all the people could hear. He read from the room of Gemariah son of Shaphan the royal secretary. This room was in the upper courtyard, near the entrance of the temple's New Gate.

decisions.choice: the chamber of Gemariah: a room on the temple court used by an official
decisions.reason: Rooms were built around the temple courts for priests, Levites and officials (35:4; 1 Chronicles 9:26). Reading from a doorway or window of such a room, Baruch could be heard by the crowd in the court.

decisions.choice: Gemariah son of Shaphan: son of King Josiah's secretary, and brother of Ahikam
decisions.reason: Shaphan was the royal secretary under Josiah who read him the book of the law (2 Kings 22:3-10). His son Ahikam had protected Jeremiah (26:24), and his family stands by the prophet again here (verses 12, 25). "The secretary" probably names Shaphan's old office, since Elishama is the secretary now (verse 12).

decisions.choice: the upper court, the New Gate: the inner court, higher than the outer, at the gate where Jeremiah was tried
decisions.reason: The inner court of the temple stood on higher ground than the outer one. The officials sat at the entrance of the New Gate to judge Jeremiah after his temple sermon (26:10).

decisions.choice: the words of Jeremiah: the same words called the words of the LORD in verse 8
decisions.reason: The words are the LORD's, given through Jeremiah; the narrator can call them by either name.

decisions.choice: chamber (L, B), room (R); the scribe (L), the secretary (B), the royal secretary (R)
decisions.reason: The royal scribe is named as in 2 Kings 22:3: Literal keeps "scribe" and Balanced and Readable name the office "secretary". Balanced puts the hearers at the end of the first sentence so that the place can be given in a sentence of its own.

source.text: וַ֠יִּשְׁמַ֗ע מִכָ֨יְהוּ בֶן־גְּמַרְיָ֧הוּ בֶן־שָׁפָ֛ן אֶת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל הַסֵּֽפֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan all [the] words of Yahweh from upon the book,

en.L: And Micaiah son of Gemariah, son of Shaphan, heard all the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the scroll,
en.B: When Micaiah son of Gemariah, son of Shaphan, heard all the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} read from the scroll,
en.R: Micaiah, the son of Gemariah and grandson of Shaphan, heard all the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that Baruch read from the scroll.

decisions.choice: the sentence goes on into verse 12
decisions.reason: Micaiah's hearing leads straight into what he did next. Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma.

decisions.choice: Micaiah: Shaphan's grandson, listening in his father's chamber
decisions.reason: Micaiah heard the reading from his father Gemariah's room (verse 10). Gemariah himself was at the palace with the other officials (verse 12).

decisions.choice: read (Balanced); that Baruch read; grandson (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says he heard the words "from upon the scroll". Balanced and Readable say they were read aloud, and Readable explains the family line.

source.text: וַיֵּ֤רֶד בֵּית־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל־לִשְׁכַּ֣ת הַסֹּפֵ֔ר וְהִ֨נֵּה־שָׁ֔ם כָּל־הַשָּׂרִ֖ים יֽוֹשְׁבִ֑ים אֱלִישָׁמָ֣ע הַסֹּפֵ֡ר וּדְלָיָ֣הוּ בֶן־שְׁ֠מַעְיָהוּ וְאֶלְנָתָ֨ן בֶּן־עַכְבּ֜וֹר וּגְמַרְיָ֧הוּ בֶן־שָׁפָ֛ן וְצִדְקִיָּ֥הוּ בֶן־חֲנַנְיָ֖הוּ וְכָל־הַשָּׂרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: and he went down [to the] house of the king, to [the] chamber of the scribe, and look, there all the princes [were] sitting: Elishama the scribe and Delaiah son of Shemaiah and Elnathan son of Achbor and Gemariah son of Shaphan and Zedekiah son of Hananiah and all the princes.

en.L: and he went down to the house of the king, to the chamber of the scribe, and look, all the princes [were] sitting there: Elishama the scribe, and Delaiah son of Shemaiah, and Elnathan son of Achbor, and Gemariah son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the princes.
en.B: he went down to the king's palace, to the secretary's chamber. All the officials were sitting there: Elishama the secretary, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah and all the other officials.
en.R: So he went down to the king's palace, to the royal secretary's room. All the leaders were meeting there: Elishama the royal secretary, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah and all the other leaders.

decisions.choice: went down: from the temple to the palace, which stood lower and to the south
decisions.reason: The palace lay just below the temple on the same ridge, so one went "down" from the temple to the palace and "up" from the palace to the temple (26:10).

decisions.choice: the princes: the king's high officials, who governed under him
decisions.reason: The word names men of rank who held office at court. They are not the king's sons; one of them is a royal secretary (Elishama).

decisions.choice: Elnathan son of Achbor; Zedekiah son of Hananiah
decisions.reason: Elnathan is the official Jehoiakim sent to Egypt to bring back the prophet Uriah (26:22); his father Achbor served Josiah (2 Kings 22:12). Zedekiah son of Hananiah is not King Zedekiah, nor is his father the prophet Hananiah of 28:1.

decisions.choice: look, there: what Micaiah found when he arrived
decisions.reason: The word often translated "behold" turns the reader's eye to what Micaiah saw: the whole council already sitting.

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R); other (B, R)
decisions.reason: This is the wording settled for this office. Balanced and Readable add "other", since the named men are among "all the officials".

source.text: וַיַּגֵּ֤ד לָהֶם֙ מִכָ֔יְהוּ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמֵ֑עַ בִּקְרֹ֥א בָר֛וּךְ בַּסֵּ֖פֶר בְּאָזְנֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And told them Micaiah all the words that he had heard when read Baruch in the book in [the] ears of the people.

en.L: And Micaiah told them all the words that he had heard when Baruch read from the scroll in the ears of the people.
en.B: Micaiah reported to them all the words he had heard when Baruch read from the scroll in the hearing of the people.
en.R: Micaiah told them everything he had heard Baruch read from the scroll to the people.

decisions.choice: told: reported, as a formal report to officials
decisions.reason: The verb is used for bringing news or a report to someone in authority (verses 16, 20). Micaiah tells the officials what was said in public.

decisions.choice: everything he had heard Baruch read ... to the people
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that Baruch read to the people, for "in the ears of the people".

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלְח֨וּ כָל־הַשָּׂרִ֜ים אֶל־בָּר֗וּךְ אֶת־יְהוּדִ֡י בֶּן־נְ֠תַנְיָהוּ בֶּן־שֶׁלֶמְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־כּוּשִׁי֮ לֵאמֹר֒ הַמְּגִלָּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר קָרָ֤אתָ בָּהּ֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם קָחֶ֥נָּה בְיָדְךָ֖ וָלֵ֑ךְ וַ֠יִּקַּח בָּר֨וּךְ בֶּן־נֵרִיָּ֤הוּ אֶת־הַמְּגִלָּה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֖א אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent all the princes to Baruch Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi, saying, The scroll which you read in it in [the] ears of the people, take it in your hand and come. And took Baruch son of Neriah the scroll in his hand and came to them.

en.L: And all the princes sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying, "The scroll from which you read in the ears of the people, take it in your hand and come." And Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
en.B: Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch to say, "Bring the scroll you read to the people, and come." So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and went to them.
en.R: Then all the leaders sent a man named Jehudi to Baruch. Jehudi was the son of Nethaniah, the grandson of Shelemiah and the great-grandson of Cushi. He told Baruch, "Bring the scroll that you read to the people, and come with me." So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll and went to the leaders.

decisions.choice: Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi: a court messenger named with three generations
decisions.reason: It is unusual to name a man's great-grandfather; it may show that Jehudi came of a known family. His name means "a Judean". Cushi is a personal name here (Zephaniah 1:1), though it can mean "a Cushite".

decisions.choice: the scroll ... take it: the scroll stands first, the thing the officials want
decisions.reason: The officials' order begins with "the scroll" and then picks it up again with "take it". They want the written words themselves, not only Micaiah's report of them.

decisions.choice: a man named; the grandson ... great-grandson; with me
decisions.reason: Readable gives the family line in a sentence of its own and says who came with whom.

decisions.choice: went to them
decisions.reason: Hebrew says Baruch "came" to the officials, from their point of view; English says he "went".

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו שֵׁ֣ב נָ֔א וּקְרָאֶ֖נָּה בְּאָזְנֵ֑ינוּ וַיִּקְרָ֥א בָר֖וּךְ בְּאָזְנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, Sit please and read it in our ears. And read Baruch in their ears.

en.L: And they said to him, "Sit down, please, and read it in our ears." And Baruch read [it] in their ears.
en.B: They said to him, "Please sit down and read it to us." So Baruch read it to them.
en.R: "Please sit down," they told him, "and read it to us." So Baruch read it to them.

decisions.choice: sit down, please: a courteous welcome
decisions.reason: The officials receive Baruch with respect and ask him to sit, as one sat to read or teach. The king will treat the scroll very differently (verses 23-24).

decisions.choice: in our ears: aloud to us
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י כְּשָׁמְעָם֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֔ים פָּחֲד֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל־בָּר֔וּךְ הַגֵּ֤יד נַגִּיד֙ לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when they heard all the words, they turned in dread each to his neighbor, and they said to Baruch, To tell we will tell the king all the words these.

en.L: And it was, when they heard all the words, [that] they turned in dread, each to his neighbor, and they said to Baruch, "We will surely tell the king all these words."
en.B: When they heard all the words, they turned to one another in alarm and said to Baruch, "We must certainly report all these words to the king."
en.R: When they heard all the words, they looked at one another in fear. They said to Baruch, "We must tell the king everything that is written here."

decisions.choice: they were in dread, each to his neighbor: they turned to one another in fear
decisions.reason: The verb of fear is joined to "each to his neighbor", picturing the men turning to look at one another in alarm (compare Genesis 42:28).

decisions.choice: we will surely tell: the officials are bound to report this to the king
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for force. The officials do not threaten Baruch; they see that words like these must reach the king, and they take care to protect Baruch and Jeremiah first (verse 19).

decisions.choice: they were afraid: the officials fear, but the king and his servants do not
decisions.reason: The same verb comes back in verse 24: "they were not afraid". The story sets the officials' fear against the king's lack of it.

decisions.choice: everything that is written here
decisions.reason: Readable says what "all these words" are: the words on the scroll.

source.text: וְאֶ֨ת־בָּר֔וּךְ שָׁאֲל֖וּ לֵאמֹ֑ר הַגֶּד־נָ֣א לָ֔נוּ אֵ֗יךְ כָּתַ֛בְתָּ אֶת־כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה מִפִּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And Baruch they asked, saying, Tell please to us, how did you write all the words these from his mouth?

en.L: And they asked Baruch, saying, "Tell us, please, how did you write all these words from his mouth?"
en.B: Then they asked Baruch, "Tell us, please, how did you come to write all these words? Was it at his dictation?"
en.R: Then they asked Baruch, "Please tell us how you wrote all this. Did Jeremiah tell you what to write?"

decisions.choice: how did you write ... from his mouth: they ask how the scroll was made and whether the words came from Jeremiah himself
alternatives: how did you write all these words that came from his mouth?
decisions.reason: "From his mouth" stands at the end of the question. The officials want to know whose words these are before they report them to the king. Baruch's answer in verse 18 picks up the same words.

decisions.choice: his: Jeremiah's, though he is not named
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's name has not been spoken in the scene, but everyone knows whose prophecy it is.

decisions.choice: a second question: Was it at his dictation? (B); Did Jeremiah tell you what to write? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make "from his mouth" a question of its own, as the order of the Hebrew suggests (m1); Literal keeps one question. Readable names Jeremiah (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ בָּר֔וּךְ מִפִּיו֙ יִקְרָ֣א אֵלַ֔י אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַאֲנִ֛י כֹּתֵ֥ב עַל־הַסֵּ֖פֶר בַּדְּיֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And said to them Baruch, From his mouth he would call out to me all the words these, and I [was] writing on the book with ink.

en.L: And Baruch said to them, "From his mouth he would call out to me all these words, and I [was] writing [them] on the scroll with ink."
en.B: Baruch answered them, "He spoke all these words aloud to me, and I wrote them down in ink on the scroll."
en.R: Baruch answered, "Jeremiah said all these words to me out loud, and I wrote them down with ink on the scroll."

decisions.choice: he would call out ... I was writing: a long process, word after word
decisions.reason: The verb forms picture an action going on over time: Jeremiah kept reciting, and Baruch kept writing.

decisions.choice: ink: the word occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible
decisions.reason: Ink was made from soot or charcoal mixed with gum and water, and written with a reed pen on leather or papyrus. Baruch's plain answer insists that he added nothing of his own.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Readable names Jeremiah for "he", as in verse 17.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ הַשָּׂרִים֙ אֶל־בָּר֔וּךְ לֵ֥ךְ הִסָּתֵ֖ר אַתָּ֣ה וְיִרְמְיָ֑הוּ וְאִ֥ישׁ אַל־יֵדַ֖ע אֵיפֹ֥ה אַתֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the princes to Baruch, Go, hide yourself, you and Jeremiah, and anyone not let know where you [are].

en.L: And the princes said to Baruch, "Go, hide yourself, you and Jeremiah, and let no one know where you [are]."
en.B: Then the officials said to Baruch, "Go and hide, you and Jeremiah. Do not let anyone know where you are."
en.R: Then the leaders told Baruch, "You and Jeremiah must go and hide. Do not let anyone know where you are."

decisions.choice: hide: the officials know the king may kill them
decisions.reason: Jehoiakim had already had the prophet Uriah brought back from Egypt and put to death for a message like Jeremiah's (26:20-23).

decisions.choice: the officials fear the words and protect the messengers
decisions.reason: Some of the king's own officials take the warning seriously. Their counsel to hide, and the LORD's hiding in verse 26, keep Baruch and Jeremiah alive.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ אֶל־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ חָצֵ֔רָה וְאֶת־הַמְּגִלָּ֣ה הִפְקִ֔דוּ בְּלִשְׁכַּ֖ת אֱלִישָׁמָ֣ע הַסֹּפֵ֑ר וַיַּגִּ֨ידוּ֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went to the king [to the] court, and the scroll they had deposited in [the] chamber of Elishama the scribe; and they told in [the] ears of the king all the words.

en.L: And they went in to the king, to the court, but the scroll they had deposited in the chamber of Elishama the scribe; and they told all the words in the ears of the king.
en.B: They went in to the king in the courtyard, having left the scroll for safekeeping in the chamber of Elishama the secretary, and they reported all the words to the king.
en.R: The leaders left the scroll in the room of Elishama the royal secretary, where it would be safe. Then they went in to the king in the courtyard and told him everything it said.

decisions.choice: they had deposited: put in someone's keeping for safety
decisions.reason: The verb is used for leaving something in trust (37:21; 40:7). The officials leave the scroll in the secretary's room before going to the king, perhaps to keep it from his hands.

decisions.choice: the court: the palace courtyard, around which the king's rooms stood
decisions.reason: The officials go in through the court to the king, who was sitting in his winter rooms (verse 22).

decisions.choice: the leaving of the scroll told first; where it would be safe
decisions.reason: The Hebrew tells the earlier action second, as an aside. Readable tells events in the order they happened and says why the scroll was left (m1).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־יְהוּדִ֗י לָקַ֨חַת֙ אֶת־הַמְּגִלָּ֔ה וַיִּ֨קָּחֶ֔הָ מִלִּשְׁכַּ֖ת אֱלִישָׁמָ֣ע הַסֹּפֵ֑ר וַיִּקְרָאֶ֤הָ יְהוּדִי֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּבְאָזְנֵי֙ כָּל־הַשָּׂרִ֔ים הָעֹמְדִ֖ים מֵעַ֥ל הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king Jehudi to take the scroll, and he took it from [the] chamber of Elishama the scribe; and read it Jehudi in [the] ears of the king and in [the] ears of all the princes the standing from upon the king.

en.L: And the king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and he took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe; and Jehudi read it in the ears of the king and in the ears of all the princes who were standing beside the king.
en.B: The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and he brought it from the chamber of Elishama the secretary. Jehudi read it to the king and to all the officials who stood in attendance on him.
en.R: So the king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and Jehudi brought it from Elishama's room. Then he read it aloud to the king and to all the leaders standing around him.

decisions.choice: standing from upon the king: standing by the seated king, ready to serve
decisions.reason: Officials stood while the king sat (verse 22); the phrase pictures attendants around a seated master (Genesis 18:8).

decisions.choice: the third reading, each closer to the king
decisions.reason: The words are read to the people (verse 10), to the officials (verse 15), and now to the king himself.

decisions.choice: stood in attendance on him
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of service in the idiom (m1); Literal says "standing beside" and Readable "standing around".

source.text: וְהַמֶּ֗לֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב֙ בֵּ֣ית הַחֹ֔רֶף בַּחֹ֖דֶשׁ הַתְּשִׁיעִ֑י וְאֶת־הָאָ֖ח לְפָנָ֥יו מְבֹעָֽרֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And the king [was] sitting [in the] house of the winter in the month the ninth, and the brazier before him [was] burning.

en.L: And the king [was] sitting in the winter house in the ninth month, and the brazier [was] burning before him.
en.B: It was the ninth month, and the king was sitting in his winter house, with a fire burning in the brazier in front of him.
en.R: It was winter, the ninth month of the year. The king was sitting in his winter rooms, and a fire was burning in a fire pot in front of him.

decisions.choice: the winter house: rooms of the palace used in the cold season
decisions.reason: Kings had separate quarters, or a separate house, for winter and for summer (Amos 3:15). The ninth month falls in November and December, when Jerusalem is cold and wet.

decisions.choice: the brazier: a pot or pan of coals for heating a room
decisions.reason: The word occurs only in this chapter (verses 22-23). It names a portable fire pot, of metal or clay, set on the floor.

decisions.choice: the brazier ... was burning: the brazier is the subject
decisions.reason: Before "the brazier" stands the small word that usually marks an object, but here the brazier is the subject of "burning". Such a use is found elsewhere in Hebrew, and the sense is clear.

decisions.choice: with a fire burning in the brazier (B); it was winter; a fire pot (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the fire burned in the brazier, which Literal has as "the brazier [was] burning". Readable says "winter" and "fire pot" in everyday words.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀כִּקְר֣וֹא יְהוּדִ֗י שָׁלֹ֣שׁ דְּלָתוֹת֮ וְאַרְבָּעָה֒ יִֽקְרָעֶ֨הָ֙ בְּתַ֣עַר הַסֹּפֵ֔ר וְהַשְׁלֵ֕ךְ אֶל־הָאֵ֖שׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶל־הָאָ֑ח עַד־תֹּם֙ כָּל־הַמְּגִלָּ֔ה עַל־הָאֵ֖שׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־הָאָֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as read Jehudi three doors and four, he would tear it with [the] knife of the scribe and throw [it] into the fire that [was] in the brazier, until was consumed all the scroll on the fire that [was] on the brazier.

en.L: And it was, as Jehudi read three columns or four, [that] he would tear it with the knife of the scribe and throw [it] into the fire that [was] in the brazier, until the whole scroll was consumed on the fire that [was] in the brazier.
en.B: Whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king would cut them away with a scribe's knife and throw them on the fire in the brazier, until the whole scroll was burned up in the fire.
en.R: Each time Jehudi finished reading three or four columns of the scroll, the king cut them off with a small knife used by scribes and threw them into the fire. He kept doing this until the whole scroll was burned up.

decisions.choice: columns: the panels of writing set side by side along a scroll
decisions.reason: The word usually means "doors". Here it names the columns of text, each like a narrow door-leaf standing beside the next as the scroll is unrolled. Some take it as sheets or pages; the sense is a section of a few columns at a time.

decisions.choice: he would tear it: the king, again and again as the reading went on
decisions.reason: The subject is not named, but verses 25 and 27-29 say that the king burned the scroll. The verbs picture a repeated act: each time a few columns were read, he cut them away.

decisions.choice: tear: the same verb as "tear" their garments in verse 24
decisions.reason: The king tore the scroll, but no one tore his clothes in grief. The play on the word is the point of the scene.

decisions.choice: the knife of the scribe: a small blade for trimming reed pens and cutting scroll material
decisions.reason: A scribe carried a small knife with his pen and ink. The king uses a writer's tool to destroy the writing.

decisions.choice: tear (L); cut them off (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "tear" so that the reader can see the same verb as in verse 24 (m3). Balanced and Readable say "cut off", since a knife was used, and name the king as the one who did it (m2).

source.text: וְלֹ֣א פָחֲד֔וּ וְלֹ֥א קָרְע֖וּ אֶת־בִּגְדֵיהֶ֑ם הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְכָל־עֲבָדָ֔יו הַשֹּׁ֣מְעִ֔ים אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And not they were afraid and not they tore their garments, the king and all his servants the hearing all the words these.

en.L: And they were not afraid, and they did not tear their garments, the king and all his servants who heard all these words.
en.B: Yet neither the king nor any of his officials who heard all these words was afraid, and they did not tear their clothes.
en.R: The king and all his officials heard all these words, but they were not afraid. They did not tear their clothes to show they were sorry.

decisions.choice: they did not tear their garments: the opposite of what Josiah, Jehoiakim's father, did
decisions.reason: When Josiah heard the words of the book of the law read by Shaphan the secretary, he tore his clothes and humbled himself (2 Kings 22:11, 19). Now a scroll is read in the presence of Shaphan's son and grandson, and Josiah's son does not tear his clothes but tears the scroll.

decisions.choice: they were not afraid: set against the officials' fear in verse 16
decisions.reason: The same verb is used. The officials who heard the words feared; the king and his servants did not.

decisions.choice: all his servants: the king's courtiers in the room, not the three officials of verse 25
decisions.reason: Verse 25 names officials who pleaded with the king, so "all his servants" here are those of his court who took his side.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: The king's servants are his court officials, as the wording for Isaiah has it; Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: to show they were sorry
decisions.reason: Readable says what tearing one's clothes meant: grief and repentance (m1).

source.text: וְגַם֩ אֶלְנָתָ֨ן וּדְלָיָ֤הוּ וּגְמַרְיָ֨הוּ֙ הִפְגִּ֣עוּ בַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְבִלְתִּ֥י שְׂרֹ֖ף אֶת־הַמְּגִלָּ֑ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And even Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, and not he listened to them.

en.L: And even Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, but he did not listen to them.
en.B: Elnathan, Delaiah and Gemariah even pleaded with the king not to burn the scroll, but he refused to listen to them.
en.R: Elnathan, Delaiah and Gemariah even begged the king not to burn the scroll, but he would not listen to them.

decisions.choice: urged: pressed the king with pleading
decisions.reason: The verb means to press upon someone, and so to plead or intercede (7:16; 27:18).

decisions.choice: Elnathan: the same official who had fetched Uriah for Jehoiakim
decisions.reason: Elnathan son of Achbor had carried out the king's order against the prophet Uriah (26:22-23). Now he joins those who plead for the scroll.

decisions.choice: refused to listen (B); would not listen (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say so because the king refused, not because he failed to hear.

source.text: וַיְצַוֶּ֣ה הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ אֶת־יְרַחְמְאֵ֨ל בֶּן־הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וְאֶת־שְׂרָיָ֣הוּ בֶן־עַזְרִיאֵ֗ל וְאֶת־שֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּֽן־עַבְדְּאֵ֔ל לָקַ֨חַת֙ אֶת־בָּר֣וּךְ הַסֹּפֵ֔ר וְאֵ֖ת יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא וַיַּסְתִּרֵ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And commanded the king Jerahmeel son of the king and Seraiah son of Azriel and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet; and hid them Yahweh.

en.L: And the king commanded Jerahmeel the son of the king, and Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel, to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet; but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hid them.
en.B: Instead, the king ordered Jerahmeel, the king's son, Seraiah son of Azriel and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and the prophet Jeremiah. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hid them.
en.R: Instead, the king ordered three men to arrest Baruch the scribe and the prophet Jeremiah. They were Jerahmeel, the king's son, Seraiah son of Azriel and Shelemiah son of Abdeel. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hid Baruch and Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: the son of the king: a prince of the royal house, or a title of a royal officer
alternatives: a royal officer with the title "king's son"
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean one of the king's sons, or a member of the royal family given police duties, as with Malchiah "the son of the king" whose cistern held Jeremiah (38:6; 1 Kings 22:26). Jehoiakim was about thirty at this time, so a grown son is possible but uncertain.

decisions.choice: Baruch the scribe: a writer by trade, Jeremiah's scribe
decisions.reason: The same word names the royal secretary (verses 10, 12). Baruch held no court office; he was a trained scribe who wrote for Jeremiah (verse 32).

decisions.choice: the LORD hid them: their safety is the LORD's doing
decisions.reason: The officials had told them to hide (verse 19), but the narrator says that it was the LORD who hid them. The king's men could not find them.

decisions.choice: the scribe
decisions.reason: Every level says "scribe" for Baruch, keeping "secretary" for the royal office in verses 10-21 (m2).

decisions.choice: three men ... They were
decisions.reason: Readable gives the order first and the names in a second sentence, and names Baruch and Jeremiah for "them".

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ אַחֲרֵ֣י׀שְׂרֹ֣ף הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֶת־הַמְּגִלָּה֙ וְאֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר כָּתַ֥ב בָּר֛וּךְ מִפִּ֥י יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to Jeremiah after burned the king the scroll and the words that wrote Baruch from [the] mouth of Jeremiah, saying:

en.L: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah after the king had burned the scroll and the words that Baruch had written from the mouth of Jeremiah, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah after the king had burned the scroll, and with it the words Baruch had written as Jeremiah dictated:
en.R: After the king burned the scroll with the words Jeremiah had spoken and Baruch had written, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah another message:

decisions.choice: the scroll and the words: the king meant to destroy the message itself
decisions.reason: The verse names both what was burned, the scroll, and what the king tried to be rid of, the words. The LORD's answer is to have the words written again.

decisions.choice: from the mouth of Jeremiah: at his dictation
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

decisions.choice: another message
decisions.reason: Readable says "another" to show that this is a new word after the burning, following the heading for "the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah".

source.text: שׁ֥וּב קַח־לְךָ֖ מְגִלָּ֣ה אַחֶ֑רֶת וּכְתֹ֣ב עָלֶ֗יהָ אֵ֤ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִים֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָי֗וּ עַל־הַמְּגִלָּה֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׂרַ֖ף יְהוֹיָקִ֥ים מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Again take for yourself [a] scroll other and write on it all the words the former that were on the scroll the first which burned Jehoiakim king of Judah.

en.L: "Again take for yourself another scroll, and write on it all the former words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.
en.B: "Take another scroll and write on it again all the words that were on the first scroll, the one that Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.
en.R: "Get another scroll. Write on it again all the words that were on the first scroll, the one King Jehoiakim of Judah burned.

decisions.choice: return, take: take again
decisions.reason: The verb "return" before another verb means doing it again. The command repeats the first one (verse 2).

decisions.choice: the former words on the first scroll: burning the scroll does not undo the message
decisions.reason: The LORD has the same words written again. What the king destroyed was leather or papyrus, not the word itself (compare Isaiah 40:8).

decisions.choice: again, placed with "write"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable attach "again" to the writing, where English expects it.

source.text: וְעַל־יְהוֹיָקִ֤ים מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ תֹּאמַ֔ר כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה אַ֠תָּה שָׂרַ֜פְתָּ אֶת־הַמְּגִלָּ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַדּוּעַ֩ כָּתַ֨בְתָּ עָלֶ֜יהָ לֵאמֹ֗ר בֹּֽא־יָב֤וֹא מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֙ וְהִשְׁחִית֙ אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וְהִשְׁבִּ֥ית מִמֶּ֖נָּה אָדָ֥ם וּבְהֵמָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say, Thus says Yahweh: You burned the scroll this, saying, Why did you write on it, saying, To come will come [the] king of Babylon and he will destroy the land this and cause to cease from it human and beast?

en.L: And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: You burned this scroll, saying, "Why did you write on it, saying, 'The king of Babylon will surely come and destroy this land and cause human and beast to cease from it'?"'
en.B: And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you are to say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: You burned this scroll and said, "Why did you write on it that the king of Babylon is sure to come and destroy this land and wipe out both people and animals from it?"'
en.R: And this is what you must say about Jehoiakim king of Judah: 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: You burned this scroll. You asked, "Why did you write that the king of Babylon will surely come and destroy this land, and kill all the people and animals in it?"'

decisions.choice: concerning Jehoiakim: a message about the king, spoken to him
decisions.reason: The preposition means "concerning" or "to". The words that follow speak to Jehoiakim directly ("you burned"), so the message is for him, whether or not it was given to him in person.

decisions.choice: saying: the king's objection, said or thought
decisions.reason: "Saying" can introduce words spoken aloud or what someone thinks. By burning the scroll Jehoiakim gave his answer to it: he rejected the warning that Babylon would come.

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon will surely come: the message of 25:8-11
decisions.reason: This sums up what Jeremiah had said in the same year: the LORD would bring Nebuchadrezzar against the land and make it a waste (25:9-11). The verb is doubled for certainty.

decisions.choice: the scroll's words reported, not quoted
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the quotation inside the king's question, with marks for each level of speech. Balanced and Readable report the scroll's words with "that", to avoid a fourth set of quotation marks.

decisions.choice: wipe out both people and animals (B); kill all the people and animals (R)
decisions.reason: To "cause to cease" people and animals from the land is to leave none alive there.

source.text: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עַל־יְהֽוֹיָקִים֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה לֹא־יִֽהְיֶה־לּ֥וֹ יוֹשֵׁ֖ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֑ד וְנִבְלָתוֹ֙ תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה מֻשְׁלֶ֔כֶת לַחֹ֥רֶב בַּיּ֖וֹם וְלַקֶּ֥רַח בַּלָּֽיְלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: Not will be to him [one] sitting on [the] throne of David, and his corpse will be thrown out to the heat by day and to the frost by night.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: There will not be for him [one] sitting on the throne of David, and his corpse will be thrown out to the heat by day and to the frost by night.
en.B: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this about Jehoiakim king of Judah: No one of his line will sit on the throne of David, and his dead body will be thrown out to the heat of the day and the frost of the night.
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: No one from his family will sit on David's throne. His dead body will be thrown out and left in the heat of the day and the frost of the night.

decisions.choice: no one to sit on the throne of David: no lasting line of kings from Jehoiakim
decisions.reason: His son Jehoiachin reigned only three months before he was taken to Babylon (2 Kings 24:8-15), and no son of Jehoiachin ruled (22:30). The throne passed to Jehoiakim's brother Zedekiah.

decisions.choice: his corpse will be thrown out: an unburied death, as 22:18-19 had said
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had said that Jehoiakim would have "the burial of a donkey", dragged out and thrown beyond the gates (22:19). The heat and frost picture a body left unburied. Kings says only that he "lay down with his fathers" (2 Kings 24:6) and does not tell how he was buried.

decisions.choice: therefore: the sentence that follows from the king's act
decisions.reason: The LORD still speaks to Jeremiah, now about Jehoiakim in the third person. Because he burned the warning, the warning will come true for him and his house.

decisions.choice: of his line (B); from his family (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the one who will not sit on the throne is someone of Jehoiakim's own line (m1).

source.text: וּפָקַדְתִּ֨י עָלָ֧יו וְעַל־זַרְע֛וֹ וְעַל־עֲבָדָ֖יו אֶת־עֲוֺנָ֑ם וְהֵבֵאתִ֣י עֲ֠לֵיהֶם וְעַל־יֹשְׁבֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם וְאֶל־אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֵ֧ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א שָׁמֵֽעוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will visit on him and on his seed and on his servants their iniquity, and I will bring on them and on [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem and to [the] men of Judah all the evil that I spoke against them, and not they listened.

en.L: And I will visit on him and on his offspring and on his servants their iniquity, and I will bring on them and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem and on the {{gender:people|men}} of Judah all the evil that I have spoken against them, and they did not listen."
en.B: I will punish him and his descendants and his officials for their guilt. I will bring on them, on those who live in Jerusalem and on the {{gender:people|men}} of Judah all the disaster I have pronounced against them, because they did not listen."
en.R: I will punish him, his children and his officials for their sin. I will bring on them, and on everyone who lives in Jerusalem and in Judah, all the disaster I warned them about, because they would not listen."

decisions.choice: visit their iniquity on him: punish him for his guilt
decisions.reason: To "visit" wrongdoing on someone is to call him to account for it and bring its punishment on him (Exodus 20:5).

decisions.choice: all the evil I have spoken: the disaster of verse 3, which the scroll was meant to turn aside
decisions.reason: The same word and phrase were used in verse 3, where the LORD hoped the people would turn. Now the "perhaps" has come to nothing.

decisions.choice: and they did not listen: the reason for the judgment
decisions.reason: The closing clause gives the cause of all that comes before it. It answers the hope of verses 3 and 7.

decisions.choice: the men of Judah: the people of Judah
decisions.reason: The word for "man" is used here for every person of Judah, as a whole people.

decisions.choice: descendants (B), children (R); officials; guilt (B), sin (R)
decisions.reason: "Seed" means offspring. The king's servants are his officials, and the word for iniquity follows the wording used for Isaiah. Literal keeps "offspring", "servants" and "iniquity".

source.text: וְיִרְמְיָ֜הוּ לָקַ֣ח׀מְגִלָּ֣ה אַחֶ֗רֶת וַֽיִּתְּנָהּ֮ אֶל־בָּר֣וּךְ בֶּן־נֵרִיָּהוּ֮ הַסֹּפֵר֒ וַיִּכְתֹּ֤ב עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ מִפִּ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י הַסֵּ֔פֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׂרַ֛ף יְהוֹיָקִ֥ים מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֖ה בָּאֵ֑שׁ וְע֨וֹד נוֹסַ֧ף עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם דְּבָרִ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים כָּהֵֽמָּה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And Jeremiah took [a] scroll other and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe, and he wrote on it from [the] mouth of Jeremiah all [the] words of the book that had burned Jehoiakim king of Judah in the fire; and yet were added to them words many like them.

en.L: And Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah, the scribe, and he wrote on it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire; and many words like them were added to them besides.
en.B: Then Jeremiah took another scroll and handed it to Baruch son of Neriah, the scribe. As Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote on it every word of the scroll that King Jehoiakim of Judah had burned in the fire, and many other words like them were added.
en.R: So Jeremiah got another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah, the scribe. Jeremiah spoke, and Baruch wrote on the new scroll all the words that had been on the scroll King Jehoiakim burned. Many more messages like them were added as well.

decisions.choice: were added: by Jeremiah through Baruch, though no one is named
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. The words came from Jeremiah, as the rest of the scroll did, and Baruch wrote them.

decisions.choice: many words like them: the second scroll held more than the first
decisions.reason: Burning the scroll did not silence the word; the new scroll was fuller. "Like them" means of the same kind: more warnings and calls to turn back.

decisions.choice: the second scroll and the book of Jeremiah
decisions.reason: This verse tells how Jeremiah's words were written down and added to. It shows part of the way the book itself took shape, though it does not say which chapters the scroll held.

decisions.choice: as Jeremiah dictated (B); Jeremiah spoke, and Baruch wrote (R); messages (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4. Readable says "messages" for "words", since whole oracles were added.
